4:T116832,<h2 id="prerequisites">Prerequisites</h2>
<p>Before starting this tutorial, make sure you have:</p>
<ul>
<li>Concerto Platform running via Docker (<span class="inline-code-block">docker-compose up -d</span>)</li>
<li>Access to <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-attr">http</span>:<span class="hljs-comment">//localhost/login</span></span> and logged in as admin</li>
<li>Read the CAT Theory document to understand IRT concepts</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="concerto-platform--known-rules-from-experience">Concerto Platform — Known Rules (From Experience)</h2>
<p>Before building, understand these important rules discovered through testing:</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Rule</th><th>Detail</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td>✅ Use <span class="odd-row"><td>✅ Enter HTML directly</td><td>Use the HTML field in <span class="inline-code-block">showPage</span>, not templates</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>✅ Use Flow variable pointers</td><td>All data ports need ↑ (output) or ↓ (input) Flow variable pointer set</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>✅ Use default <span class="inline-code-block">out</span> port</td><td>Do not use custom branch names or <span class="inline-code-block">.branch</span></td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>✅ Use <span class="inline-code-block">if</span> node with variable</td><td>Pass a <span <span class="inline-code-block">table=</span> argument</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>❌ No custom <span class="inline-code-block">.branch</span> names</td><td>Custom execution ports with <span class="inline-code-block">.branch</span> don't work reliably</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>❌ No <span class="inline-code-block">form</span> node</td><td>Variables don't pass through correctly</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>❌ No <span class="inline-code-block">table=</span> argument</td><td><span class="inline-code-block">concerto.<span class="hljs-property">table</span>.<span <h2 id="concept-what-is-the-3pl-model-with-guessing">Concept: What is the 3PL Model (with Guessing)?</h2>

<p>Where:</p>
<ul>
<li><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span></span></span></span> <span class="strong-block">(theta)</span> — test-taker's ability estimate (starts at 0)</li>
<li><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">a</span></span></span></span></span> — discrimination: how well the item separates ability levels</li>
<li><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">b</span></span></span></span></span> — difficulty: the ability level at which <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6833em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.1389em;">P</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.5</span></span></span></span></span> (ignoring guessing)</li>
<li><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span></span></span></span></span> — guessing: minimum probability of correct answer (e.g. 0.25 for 4-choice MCQ)</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="why-does-guessing-matter">Why does guessing matter?</h3>
<p>Without guessing (2PL), if theta is very low, <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.1389em;">P</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">correct</span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">→</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span></span>. But in reality, a test-taker can still guess correctly — especially on multiple choice. The guessing parameter <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span></span></span></span></span> sets a <span class="strong-block">floor</span> on the probability <a href="#ref-2">[2]</a>:</p>
<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.5604em;vertical-align:-0.8104em;"></span><span class="mop op-limits"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.6944em;"><span style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mrel mtight">→</span><span class="mord mtight">−</span><span class="mord mtight">∞</span></span></span></span><span style="top:-3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span><span class="mop">lim</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8104em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.1389em;">P</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.1389em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.5806em;vertical-align:-0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">0.25</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:1em;"></span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">(for 4-choice MCQ)</span></span></span></span></span></span></div>

style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.1389em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.936em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span></span></span></span></span></div>
<p>Items with <span class="strong-block">high discrimination (<span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">a</span></span></span></span></span>)</span> and <span class="strong-block">difficulty near current theta (<span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">b</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span></span></span></span>)</span> provide the most information <a href="#ref-3">[3]</a><a href="#ref-14">[14]</a>.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="concept-bayesian-eap-theta-estimation">Concept: Bayesian EAP Theta Estimation</h2>
<p>This tutorial uses <span class="strong-block">Bayesian Expected A Posteriori (EAP)</span> estimation — the most robust method for CAT theta estimation <a href="#ref-8">[8]</a><a href="#ref-10">[10]</a>.</p>
<h3 id="why-bayesian-eap-instead-of-newton-raphson">Why Bayesian EAP instead of Newton-Raphson?</h3>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Method</th><th>Pro</th><th>Con</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td>Newton-Raphson</td><td>Fast, simple</td><td>Undefined when all answers correct or all incorrect; can diverge <a href="#ref-9" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">[9]</a></td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>Bayesian EAP</td><td>Works for all response patterns; stable; provides SE <a href="#ref-8" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">[8]</a></td><td>Slightly biased toward prior in early items <a href="#ref-10" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">[10]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<h3 id="how-eap-works">How EAP Works</h3>
<p>EAP combines the <span class="strong-block">likelihood</span> of the observed responses with a <span class="strong-block">prior distribution</span> (our belief about ability before the test) <a href="#ref-8">[8]</a>:</p>

<h3 id="numerical-approximation-used-in-our-r-code">Numerical Approximation (used in our R code)</h3>
<p>The integral is approximated using <span class="strong-block">Gauss-Hermite quadrature</span> — evaluating the integrand at a grid of <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span <div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" <h2 id="part-1-create-the-item-bank-data-table">Part 1: Create the Item Bank (Data Table)</h2>
<h3 id="concept">Concept</h3>
<p>The item bank stores all test questions along with their IRT parameters. The <span class="strong-block">3PL model</span> requires three parameters per item: discrimination (<span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">a</span></span></span></span></span>), difficulty (<span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">b</span></span></span></span></span>), and guessing (<span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span></span></span></span></span>) <a href="#ref-2">[2]</a><a href="#ref-5">[5]</a><a href="#ref-15">[15]</a>.</p>
<h3 id="steps">Steps</h3>
<ol>
<li>Click <span class="strong-block">Data Tables</span> in the left menu → <span class="strong-block">Add new</span></li>
<li>Name it <span class="inline-code-block">item_bank_3pl</span></li>
<li>Add these columns by clicking <span class="strong-block">Add column</span>:</li>
</ol>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Column Name</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">question</span></td><td>string</td><td>The question text</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">option_a</span></td><td>string</td><td>Choice A</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">option_b</span></td><td>string</td><td>Choice B</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">option_c</span></td><td>string</td><td>Choice C</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">option_d</span></td><td>string</td><td>Choice D</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">correct_answer</span></td><td>string</td><td>Correct option: A, B, C, or D</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">difficulty</span></td><td>decimal</td><td>IRT <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">b</span></span></span></span></span> parameter (range: -3 to +3)</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">discrimination</span></td><td>decimal</td><td>IRT <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">a</span></span></span></span></span> parameter (range: 0 to 3)</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">guessing</span></td><td>decimal</td><td>IRT <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span></span></span></span></span> parameter (range: 0 to 0.35)</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<ol start="4">
<li>Click <span class="strong-block">Save</span></li>
<li>Click <span class="strong-block">Edit data</span> and add sample items with varying difficulty:</li>
</ol>

<ol start="6">
<li>Click <span class="strong-block">Save</span></li>
</ol>
<blockquote>
<p><span class="strong-block">Note:</span> All guessing values are 0.25 because these are 4-choice MCQ items. The probability of guessing correctly = 1/4 = 0.25.</p>

<h2 id="node-1-eval---init--initialize-variables">Node 1: <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - init</span> — Initialize Variables</h2>
<h3 id="concept-1">Concept</h3>
<p>This node sets all starting values before the test begins. For Bayesian EAP, we also initialize:</p>
<ul>
<li><span class="inline-code-block">responses</span> — a vector tracking all responses (1=correct, 0=incorrect) across items</li>
<li><span class="inline-code-block">items_a</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">items_b</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">items_c</span> — vectors tracking IRT parameters of answered items</li>
<li><span class="inline-code-block">se_theta</span> — the standard error of the theta estimate</li>
<li><span class="inline-code-block">theta = 0</span> — prior mean (start at average ability) <a href="#ref-12">[12]</a></li>
</ul>
<p>The response history vectors are essential for EAP because it needs <span class="strong-block">all previous responses and item parameters</span> to compute the posterior, not just the most recent one <a href="#ref-8">[8]</a>.</p>
<h3 id="steps-1">Steps</h3>
<ol>
<li>Right-click canvas → <span class="strong-block">eval</span></li>
<li>Rename it to <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - init</span></li>
<li>Click the node → edit <span class="strong-block">Code</span> field → paste:</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="connect">Connect</h3>
<p>Drag from <span class="inline-code-block">test start</span> <span class="strong-block">out</span> → <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - init</span> <span class="strong-block">in</span></p>
<h3 id="details">Details</h3>
<p>The <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - init</span> node runs <span class="strong-block">exactly once</span> — at the very beginning of the test, immediately after <span class="inline-code-block">test start</span>. Its sole purpose is to <span class="strong-block">initialize every variable</span> that will be used throughout the entire CAT session.</p>
<p>It is the simplest node in the flow but also the most foundational: if any variable is missing or wrongly typed here, every subsequent node will fail.</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Property</th><th>Value</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Runs</span></td><td>Once only — at test start</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Position in flow</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block">test start</span> → <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - init</span> → <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - select item</span></td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Purpose</span></td><td>Initialize all session variables with correct types and starting values</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Outputs</span></td><td>All variables needed by every other node</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>

<h4 id="variable-by-variable-explanation">Variable-by-Variable Explanation</h4>
<hr>
<h5 id="theta---0"><span class="inline-code-block">theta &lt;- 0</span></h5>
<p><span class="strong-block">What it is:</span>
The current ability estimate <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.9579em;"></span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.9579em;"><span style="top:-3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span><span style="top:-3.2634em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left:-0.1667em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> — the CAT's best guess of the test-taker's true latent ability on the IRT scale.</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why start at 0:</span>
In IRT, the ability scale is standardized so that the <span class="strong-block">population mean is 0</span> and the standard deviation is 1. Starting at <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.1079em;vertical-align:-0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.9579em;"><span style="top:-3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span><span style="top:-3.2634em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left:-0.1667em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3011em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0278em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">0</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span></span> means we begin with the assumption that the test-taker has average ability — the most neutral and statistically justified starting point before any evidence is collected.</p>
<p>This is the <span class="strong-block">prior mean</span> of the Bayesian EAP estimation. The standard normal prior <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0359em;">π</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathcal" style="margin-right:0.1474em;">N</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> used in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span> is centered at 0, so starting theta at 0 is consistent with the prior.</p>
<p><span class="strong-block">What happens if we started elsewhere:</span></p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why 999 and not 0, NA, or Inf:</span></p>
<p>Before any items are answered (<span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">n</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span></span>), the true SE is mathematically infinite:</p>
<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6833em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">S</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">E</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:2.2514em;vertical-align:-0.93em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:1.3214em;"><span style="top:-2.2028em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord sqrt"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.9072em;"><span class="svg-align" style="top:-3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord" style="padding-left:0.833em;"><span class="mord">0</span></span></span><span style="top:-2.8672em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="hide-tail" style="min-width:0.853em;height:1.08em;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="400em" height="1.08em" viewBox="0 0 400000 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMin slice"><path d="M95,702

<p>We cannot use <span class="inline-code-block">Inf</span> directly because Concerto may corrupt infinite values during flow variable serialization. <span class="inline-code-block">999</span> is a <span class="strong-block">sentinel value</span> — a deliberately large finite number that means "infinitely uncertain":</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Value</th><th>Problem</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">Inf</span></td><td>May not serialize correctly through Concerto flow pointers</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">NA</span></td><td>Causes arithmetic errors in CI calculation: <span class="inline-code-block">0 ± 1.96 * NA</span> → <span class="inline-code-block">NA</span></td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">0</span></td><td>Implies perfect precision — dangerously wrong</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">999</span></td><td>✅ Safely serializable, obviously not a real SE, makes all stopping rules evaluate correctly</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>

<p><span class="strong-block">How SE evolves:</span></p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>After item</th><th>Typical SE</th><th>Interpretation</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td>0 (init)</td><td><span class="strong-block">999</span></td><td>Sentinel — no data</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>1</td><td>~0.89</td><td>Very uncertain</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>3</td><td>~0.62</td><td>Improving</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>5</td><td>~0.48</td><td>Acceptable</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>7</td><td>~0.38</td><td>Good</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>10</td><td>~0.31</td><td>High precision</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<p>SE is a real EAP-computed value from item 1 onward — <span class="inline-code-block">999</span> exists only for the single moment before the first item is shown.</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why start at 0:</span>
No items have been answered at test start. This counter increments by 1 in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span> after each submission:</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">How it is used:</span></p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Node</th><th>Use of <span class="inline-code-block">answered</span></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">showPage - question</span></td><td>Displays "Question {{answered}} of {{max_items}}"</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span></td><td>Incremented after each response</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span></td><td>Used in stopping rule: <span class="inline-code-block">n_answered &gt;= max_items</span></td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">showPage - result</span></td><td>Shows total items answered</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - compute result</span></td><td>Used for percentage correct calculation</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<p><span class="strong-block">Why integer not logical:</span>
<span class="inline-code-block">answered</span> participates in arithmetic (<span class="inline-code-block">answered + 1</span>) and comparison (<span class="inline-code-block">answered &gt;= max_items</span>), so it must be numeric. Starting as <span class="inline-code-block">0</span> (integer) ensures this.</p>

      ↓

                 test_complete &lt;- n_answered &gt;= max_items</code></pre>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why defined here and not hardcoded in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span>:</span>
Centralizing configuration in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - init</span> means you only need to change one place to adjust test length. If it were hardcoded in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span>, you would need to update two nodes whenever you changed the test length.</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why <span class="inline-code-block">numeric(0)</span> and not <span class="inline-code-block">c()</span> or <span class="inline-code-block">NULL</span>:</span></p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Initialization</th><th>Type</th><th>Problem</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">c()</span></td><td>NULL</td><td><span class="inline-code-block">length(NULL) = 0</span> works, but type is ambiguous</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">NULL</span></td><td>NULL</td><td><span class="inline-code-block">c(NULL, 5)</span> → <span class="inline-code-block">5</span> but Concerto may serialize NULL differently</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">numeric(0)</span></td><td><span class="strong-block">numeric</span></td><td>✅ Explicitly numeric, empty vector of correct type</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<p>Using <span class="inline-code-block">numeric(0)</span> ensures that when we later do <span class="inline-code-block">c(used_items, current_id)</span> where <span class="inline-code-block">current_id</span> is an integer, the result is always a numeric vector — never a character or list.</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why this is critical for Bayesian EAP:</span>
Unlike Newton-Raphson (which uses only the most recent item), EAP recomputes theta from scratch after every item using <span class="strong-block">all previous responses</span>. Without this vector, EAP cannot function — it needs the complete response history to compute the likelihood.</p>
<p><span class="strong-block">Why <span class="inline-code-block">numeric(0)</span> not <span class="inline-code-block">c()</span>:</span>
Same reasoning as <span class="inline-code-block">used_items</span> — explicit numeric type prevents type errors when arithmetic is performed on elements in the EAP loop.</p>

<h5 id="items_a---numeric0-items_b---numeric0-items_c---numeric0"><span class="inline-code-block">items_a &lt;- numeric(0)</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">items_b &lt;- numeric(0)</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">items_c &lt;- numeric(0)</span></h5>
<p><span class="strong-block">What they are:</span>
Three parallel vectors that store the IRT parameters of every item that has been answered, in the same order as <span class="inline-code-block">responses</span>.</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why this is separate from theta:</span>
<span class="inline-code-block">total_correct</span> is a classical test theory metric (raw score / percentage correct). Theta is an IRT metric. They measure the same construct differently:</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>Type</th><th>Range</th><th>Properties</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">total_correct</span></td><td>Classical</td><td>0 to <span class="inline-code-block">max_items</span></td><td>Simple count, scale-dependent</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">theta</span></td><td>IRT</td><td><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">−</span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span></span> to <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">+</span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span></span></td><td>Scale-independent, comparable across test forms</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<p>Both are reported on the results page to give test-takers a familiar score alongside the IRT estimate.</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why logical not integer:</span>
The <span class="inline-code-block">if</span> node expression field expects a logical (<span class="inline-code-block">TRUE</span>/<span class="inline-code-block">FALSE</span>) value. If <span class="inline-code-block">test_complete</span> were an integer (<span class="inline-code-block">0</span> or <span class="inline-code-block">1</span>), the <span class="inline-code-block">if</span> node might not evaluate it correctly. Initializing as <span class="inline-code-block">FALSE</span> (logical) and keeping it as logical throughout avoids this issue.</p>
<hr>
<h4 id="why-every-variable-must-be-initialized-here">Why Every Variable Must Be Initialized Here</h4>
<p>Concerto flow variable pointers only work for variables that <span class="strong-block">already exist</span> in the R session. If a variable is first created in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - select item</span> or <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span> (instead of <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - init</span>), it will not be available as a flow variable in earlier rounds when the loop returns to that node.</p>
<p>The pattern is:</p>

      ↓
eval - select item reads some, overwrites some, passes all forward
      ↓

      ↓

<p>If any variable is missing from <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - init</span>, the first time the loop returns to <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - select item</span>, that variable will be <span class="inline-code-block">NULL</span> — causing either a silent error or a crash.</p>
<hr>
<h4 id="type-choices--why-they-matter">Type Choices — Why They Matter</h4>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Variable</th><th>Type</th><th>Why this type</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr <hr>
<h4 id="summary">Summary</h4>
<p><span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - init</span> is the <span class="strong-block">configuration and initialization hub</span> of the entire CAT session. Its design principles are:</p>
<ol>
<li><span class="strong-block">Initialize everything</span> — every variable used anywhere in the flow must be created here with the correct type</li>
<li><span class="strong-block">Use safe types</span> — <span class="inline-code-block">numeric(0)</span> for empty vectors, <span class="inline-code-block">FALSE</span> for logicals, <span class="inline-code-block">0</span> for numeric counters</li>
<li><span class="strong-block">Use sentinel values</span> — <span class="inline-code-block">se_theta = 999</span> for "not yet computed" infinity</li>
<li><span class="strong-block">Centralize configuration</span> — <span class="inline-code-block">max_items = 10</span> here means one place to change test length</li>
<li><span class="strong-block">Export everything</span> — every variable needs an output port with Flow variable pointer (↑)</li>
</ol>
<hr>
<h2 id="node-2-eval---select-item--cat-item-selection-3pl-maximum-information">Node 2: <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - select item</span> — CAT Item Selection (3PL Maximum Information)</h2>
<h3 id="concept-2">Concept</h3>

<h3 id="connect-1">Connect</h3>
<p>Drag from <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - init</span> <span class="strong-block">out</span> → <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - select item</span> <span class="strong-block">in</span></p>
<h3 id="details-1">Details</h3>
<p>The <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - select item</span> node runs <span class="strong-block">at the start of every CAT loop iteration</span> — once before each question is shown. It is the implementation of the <span class="strong-block">CAT item selection algorithm</span>: given the current ability estimate <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.9579em;"></span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.9579em;"><span style="top:-3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span><span style="top:-3.2634em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left:-0.1667em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>, it selects the most informative unused item from the bank.</p>
<p>It performs four sequential tasks:</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Task</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Task 1</span></td><td>Load all items from the database</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Task 2</span></td><td>Filter out already-used items</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Task 3</span></td><td>Compute 3PL information for each remaining item</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Task 4</span></td><td>Select the item with maximum information and set display variables</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>

<h5 id="what-it-does">What it does</h5>
<p>Queries the entire <span class="inline-code-block">item_bank_3pl</span> table and returns all rows as an R data frame stored in <span class="inline-code-block">items</span>.</p>
<h5 id="why-select-">Why <span class="inline-code-block">SELECT *</span></h5>
<p>We need all columns — question text, options, correct answer, and IRT parameters — so <span class="inline-code-block">SELECT *</span> retrieves everything in one call. A more targeted query like <span class="inline-code-block">SELECT id, discrimination, difficulty, guessing</span> would be faster for large banks, but for typical CAT banks of 50–200 items the difference is negligible.</p>
<h5 id="what-items-looks-like-after-this-line">What <span class="inline-code-block">items</span> looks like after this line</h5>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>id</th><th>question</th><th>option_a</th><th>option_b</th><th>option_c</th><th>option_d</th><th>correct_answer</th><th>difficulty</th><th>discrimination</th><th>guessing</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td>1</td><td>What is 1+1?</td><td>1</td><td>2</td><td>3</td><td>4</td><td>B</td><td>-2.0</td><td>0.8</td><td>0.25</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>2</td><td>What is 5-3?</td><td>1</td><td>2</td><td>3</td><td>4</td><td>B</td><td>-1.5</td><td>1.0</td><td>0.25</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>3</td><td>What is 4x3?</td><td>10</td><td>12</td><td>14</td><td>16</td><td>B</td><td>-1.0</td><td>1.2</td><td>0.25</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>...</td><td>...</td><td>...</td><td>...</td><td>...</td><td>...</td><td>...</td><td>...</td><td>...</td><td>...</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>10</td><td>What is log₂(256)?</td><td>6</td><td>7</td><td>8</td><td>9</td><td>C</td><td>2.5</td><td>2.0</td><td>0.25</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<h5 id="data-types-from-concerto-database">Data types from Concerto database</h5>
<p>Concerto returns all database values as <span class="strong-block">character strings</span> by default, regardless of the column type declared in the Data Table. This is why explicit type conversion is always required before any mathematical operations.</p>

<h5 id="lengthused_items--0"><span class="inline-code-block">length(used_items) &gt; 0</span></h5>
<p>Checks whether any items have already been administered. On the <span class="strong-block">very first question</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">used_items</span> was initialized as <span class="inline-code-block">numeric(0)</span> (an empty vector) in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - init</span>, so <span class="inline-code-block">length(numeric(0)) = 0</span> and the filter block is <span class="strong-block">skipped entirely</span> — all items remain available.</p>
<p>From question 2 onward, <span class="inline-code-block">used_items</span> grows by one ID per answered item, so the filter runs.</p>

<h5 id="items-"><span class="inline-code-block">items[..., ]</span></h5>
<p>Subsets the data frame — keeping only rows where the logical vector is <span class="inline-code-block">TRUE</span>:</p>

<span class="hljs-comment"># → c(0.969, 0.938, 0.625, 0.312, 0.254)</span></code></pre>
          </div>

<p>This is equivalent to running a for-loop over all items but is:</p>
<ul>
<li><span class="strong-block">Faster</span> — implemented in compiled C internally</li>
<li><span class="strong-block">Cleaner</span> — no loop boilerplate</li>
<li><span class="strong-block">Less error-prone</span> — no index management</li>
</ul>

<p>The difficulty parameter <span class="strong-block">shifts the curve left or right</span> along the theta axis. At <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8444em;vertical-align:-0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">b</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> (ignoring guessing, <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span></span>):</p>

<p>Note: <span class="inline-code-block">pmax</span>/<span class="inline-code-block">pmin</span> (lowercase p) operate <span class="strong-block">element-wise on vectors</span>, unlike <span class="inline-code-block">max</span>/<span class="inline-code-block">min</span> which return a single scalar. This is important here since <span class="inline-code-block">P</span> is a vector of 10 values.</p>

<h6 id="component-1-span-classmath-placeholder-data-mid153span--discrimination-squared">Component 1: <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.0728em;vertical-align:-0.2587em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">a</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-2.4413em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2587em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> — Discrimination squared</h6>

An item with <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">a</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">2.0</span></span></span></span></span> provides <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">4</span><span class="mord">×</span></span></span></span></span> more information (at its peak) than one with <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">a</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">1.0</span></span></span></span></span>.</p>

<p>So the guessing parameter reduces peak information by factor <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">−</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.0641em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose"><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>. For <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.25</span></span></span></span></span>: reduction factor = <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.0641em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">0.75</span><span class="mclose"><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.5625</span></span></span></span></span> — guessing cuts peak information nearly in half.</p>
<h6 id="component-3-span-classmath-placeholder-data-mid166span--uncertainty-term">Component 3: <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span <p>This term is maximized when <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8333em;vertical-align:-0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.1389em;">P</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.1389em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.5</span></span></span></span></span> and approaches 0 at both extremes:</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Combined with the guessing correction</span>, the true maximum information for a 3PL item occurs slightly <span class="strong-block">above</span> the difficulty parameter <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8444em;vertical-align:-0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">b</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>, not exactly at it, because the guessing floor shifts the optimal point upward.</p>

<h5 id="what-it-does-1">What it does</h5>
<p>Appends <span class="inline-code-block">current_id</span> to the <span class="inline-code-block">used_items</span> vector, recording that this item has been administered.</p>
<h5 id="why-this-must-happen-in-eval---select-item-not-eval---score">Why this must happen in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - select item</span> not <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span></h5>
<p>The item ID must be tracked <span class="strong-block">before</span> the item is shown, not after it is scored. If the test-taker closes the browser mid-question (after seeing but before submitting), the <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span> node never runs. Tracking in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - select item</span> ensures the item is always recorded as used even in this edge case.</p>

<p>This vector is passed back via output flow variable pointer (↑) so the <span class="strong-block">next iteration</span> of <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - select item</span> can filter it out.</p>
<hr>
<h4 id="how-item-selection-adapts-across-the-test">How Item Selection Adapts Across the Test</h4>
<p>The key insight is that <span class="inline-code-block">theta</span> changes after every item (updated by <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span>), and <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - select item</span> always uses the <span class="strong-block">latest</span> <span class="inline-code-block">theta</span>. This creates the adaptive cycle:</p>

          <div class="code-block">
          <div class="title-code">
            <span class="title-code-text"><svg class="lang-icon-fallback" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M7 15l5-5-5-5M13 19h6" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg></span>
            <div class="code-actions">
              <button class="wrap-code" data-code-id="cvyncp" aria-label="Toggle word wrap">
                <svg class="h-6 w-6" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                  <path d="M3 6h18M3 12h15a3 3 0 1 1 0 6h-4m0 0 2-2m-2 2 2 2M3 18h7" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/>

          <div class="pre-code">
          <pre><code id="cvyncp" class="">Round 1: theta = 0.0  → select item with b closest to 0.0 → item 5 (b=0.0)
         Test-taker answers CORRECTLY
         EAP update: theta = 0.38

Round 2: theta = 0.38 → select item with max I(0.38) from remaining 9 items
         → item 6 (b=0.5) now optimal (closest to 0.38)
         Test-taker answers INCORRECTLY
         EAP update: theta = 0.15

Round 3: theta = 0.15 → select item with max I(0.15) from remaining 8 items
         → item 6 already used, next best is item 4 (b=-0.5) or item 5 (b=0.0)
         ...</code></pre>
          </div>
          </div>
        
<p>The test converges on the true ability through this iterative approximation process.</p>
<hr>
<h4 id="why-maximum-information-is-the-right-criterion">Why Maximum Information is the Right Criterion</h4>
<h5 id="fisher-information-and-theta-estimation">Fisher Information and theta estimation</h5>
<p>The <span class="strong-block">Fisher Information</span> is the expected value of the squared score function:</p>
<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathcal" style="margin-right:0.0738em;">I</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:3em;vertical-align:-1.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">E</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="minner"><span class="mopen delimcenter" style="top:0em;"><span class="delimsizing size4">[</span></span><span class="minner"><span class="minner"><span class="mopen delimcenter" style="top:0em;"><span class="delimsizing size3">(</span></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:1.3714em;"><span style="top:-2.314em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord" style="margin-right:0.0556em;">∂</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span></span><span style="top:-3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width:0.04em;"></span></span><span style="top:-3.677em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord" style="margin-right:0.0556em;">∂</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.686em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mop">lo<span style="margin-right:0.0139em;">g</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="mclose delimcenter" style="top:0em;"><span class="delimsizing size3">)</span></span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:1.654em;"><span style="top:-3.9029em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose delimcenter" style="top:0em;"><span class="delimsizing size4">]</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></div>
<p>For IRT, this simplifies to the Item Information Function <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0785em;">I</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0785em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span>. The <span class="strong-block">Cramér-Rao lower bound</span> states that no unbiased estimator can have variance smaller than:</p>
<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.2079em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">Var</span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.9579em;"><span style="top:-3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span><span style="top:-3.2634em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left:-0.1667em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≥</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:2.3072em;vertical-align:-0.9857em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:1.3214em;"><span style="top:-2.314em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mop"><span class="mop op-symbol small-op" style="position:relative;top:0em;">∑</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.162em;"><span style="top:-2.4003em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2997em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0785em;">I</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0785em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span><span style="top:-3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width:0.04em;"></span></span><span style="top:-3.677em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.9857em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span></span></span></span></span></div>
<p>Therefore, <span class="strong-block">maximizing the total information <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.0497em;vertical-align:-0.2997em;"></span><span class="mop"><span class="mop op-symbol small-op" style="position:relative;top:0em;">∑</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.162em;"><span style="top:-2.4003em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2997em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0785em;">I</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0785em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> minimizes the estimation variance</span>. By selecting the item with the highest <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.2079em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0785em;">I</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0785em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.9579em;"><span style="top:-3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span><span style="top:-3.2634em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left:-0.1667em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> at each step, CAT greedily minimizes the variance of the final theta estimate with each question.</p>

<p>For our 10-item demonstration CAT, Maximum Information is appropriate. For operational CATs with security requirements, exposure control methods (Sympson-Hetter, randomesque) are preferred.</p>

<h2 id="node-3-showpage---question--display-question">Node 3: <span class="inline-code-block">showPage - question</span> — Display Question</h2>

<h2 id="node-4-eval---score--score-response--bayesian-eap-theta-estimation">Node 4: <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span> — Score Response + Bayesian EAP Theta Estimation</h2>
<h3 id="concept-4">Concept</h3>
<p>This is the most important node. It performs three tasks after each response:</p>
<p><span class="strong-block">Task 1 — Score the response</span></p>
<p>Compare the submitted answer to <span class="inline-code-block">correct_answer</span>:</p>
<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.5806em;vertical-align:-0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">u</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.1514em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">n</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:3em;vertical-align:-1.25em;"></span><span class="minner"><span class="mopen delimcenter" style="top:0em;"><span class="delimsizing size4">{</span></span><span class="mord"><span class="mtable"><span class="col-align-l"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:1.69em;"><span style="top:-3.69em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3.008em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">1</span></span></span><span style="top:-2.25em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3.008em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:1.19em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="arraycolsep" style="width:1em;"></span><span class="col-align-l"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:1.69em;"><span style="top:-3.69em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3.008em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">if answer is correct</span></span></span></span><span style="top:-2.25em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3.008em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">if answer is incorrect</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:1.19em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span></span></span></span></span></div>
<p><span class="strong-block">Task 2 — Update theta using Bayesian EAP</span></p>
<p>EAP treats theta estimation as a Bayesian inference problem <a href="#ref-8">[8]</a>. After collecting <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">n</span></span></span></span></span> responses <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4444em;"></span><span class="mord mathbf">u</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">u</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3011em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="minner">…</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">u</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">n</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" <p><span class="strong-block">(a) Compute the likelihood</span> of observing all responses at each grid point <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8444em;vertical-align:-0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3361em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0278em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.0315em;">k</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>:</p>
<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" <h3 id="why-eap-is-better-for-cat">Why EAP is Better for CAT</h3>
<ul>
<li><span class="strong-block">Works for all response patterns</span> — including all-correct or all-incorrect (Newton-Raphson fails here) <a href="#ref-8">[8]</a><a href="#ref-9">[9]</a></li>
<li><span class="strong-block">Provides SE</span> — we know how precise our estimate is at each step <a href="#ref-8">[8]</a></li>
<li><span class="strong-block">Stable</span> — bounded by the prior; never diverges to ±∞ <a href="#ref-10">[10]</a></li>
<li><span class="strong-block">Uses all response history</span> — not just the last item <a href="#ref-8">[8]</a></li>
</ul>

          <pre><code id="pzueom" class="r"><span class="hljs-comment"># ── Task 1: Score the response ────────────────────────────────────────────────</span>
