<span class="hljs-comment"># ── Task 2: Bayesian EAP Theta Estimation ─────────────────────────────────────</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">#</span>
<span class="hljs-comment"># We approximate the posterior integral using a discrete quadrature grid.</span>
<span class="hljs-comment"># The grid spans [-4, 4] with K=41 equally-spaced points.</span>
<span class="hljs-comment"># This range covers &gt;99.99% of the standard normal prior.</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">#</span>
<span class="hljs-comment"># Formula:</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">#   θ̂_EAP = Σ(θ_k * w_k) / Σ(w_k)</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">#   SE_EAP = sqrt(Σ((θ_k - θ̂)² * w_k) / Σ(w_k))</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">#</span>
<span class="hljs-comment"># where w_k = L(θ_k | u) * π(θ_k)</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">#       L(θ_k | u) = likelihood of all responses at θ_k</span>
<span class="hljs-comment">#       π(θ_k)     = standard normal prior PDF</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># Step 2a: Define the quadrature grid</span>
K        <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> 41                          <span class="hljs-comment"># number of grid points</span>
theta_grid <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> seq<span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span><span class="hljs-operator">-</span><span class="hljs-number">4</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">,</span> <span class="hljs-number">4</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">,</span> length.out <span class="hljs-operator">=</span> K<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>  <span class="hljs-comment"># θ_k values</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># Step 2b: Compute log-likelihood at each grid point</span>
<span class="hljs-comment"># For each θ_k, sum log-likelihoods across all answered items</span>
log_lik <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> numeric<span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>K<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>

<span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>k <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">seq_len</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>K<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">{</span>
  th <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> theta_grid<span class="hljs-punctuation">[</span>k<span class="hljs-punctuation">]</span>
  ll <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> 0

  <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>j <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">seq_len</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>answered<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">{</span>
    <span class="hljs-comment"># 3PL probability for item j at grid point θ_k</span>
    Pj <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> items_c<span class="hljs-punctuation">[</span>j<span class="hljs-punctuation">]</span> <span class="hljs-operator">+</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span><span class="hljs-number">1</span> <span class="hljs-operator">-</span> items_c<span class="hljs-punctuation">[</span>j<span class="hljs-punctuation">]</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span> <span class="hljs-operator">/</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span><span class="hljs-number">1</span> <span class="hljs-operator">+</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">exp</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span><span class="hljs-operator">-</span>items_a<span class="hljs-punctuation">[</span>j<span class="hljs-punctuation">]</span> <span class="hljs-operator">*</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>th <span class="hljs-operator">-</span> items_b<span class="hljs-punctuation">[</span>j<span class="hljs-punctuation">]</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>

    <span class="hljs-comment"># Safety clamp to avoid log(0)</span>
    Pj <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">max</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span><span class="hljs-built_in">min</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>Pj<span class="hljs-punctuation">,</span> <span class="hljs-number">0.9999</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">,</span> <span class="hljs-number">0.0001</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>

    <span class="hljs-comment"># Add log-likelihood contribution of this item&#x27;s response</span>
    <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>responses<span class="hljs-punctuation">[</span>j<span class="hljs-punctuation">]</span> <span class="hljs-operator">==</span> <span class="hljs-number">1</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">{</span>
      ll <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> ll <span class="hljs-operator">+</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">log</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>Pj<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>
    <span class="hljs-punctuation">}</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">else</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">{</span>
      ll <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> ll <span class="hljs-operator">+</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">log</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span><span class="hljs-number">1</span> <span class="hljs-operator">-</span> Pj<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>
    <span class="hljs-punctuation">}</span>
  <span class="hljs-punctuation">}</span>

  log_lik<span class="hljs-punctuation">[</span>k<span class="hljs-punctuation">]</span> <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> ll
<span class="hljs-punctuation">}</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># Step 2c: Exponentiate log-likelihood (numerically stable via centering)</span>
<span class="hljs-comment"># Subtract max log-lik before exp to prevent overflow/underflow</span>
log_lik_centered <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> log_lik <span class="hljs-operator">-</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">max</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>log_lik<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>
likelihood       <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">exp</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>log_lik_centered<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># Step 2d: Apply standard normal prior π(θ_k) = φ(θ_k)</span>
prior   <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> dnorm<span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>theta_grid<span class="hljs-punctuation">,</span> mean <span class="hljs-operator">=</span> <span class="hljs-number">0</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">,</span> sd <span class="hljs-operator">=</span> <span class="hljs-number">1</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># Step 2e: Compute unnormalized posterior weights</span>
weights <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> likelihood <span class="hljs-operator">*</span> prior

<span class="hljs-comment"># Step 2f: Normalize weights so they sum to 1</span>
weights_sum      <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">sum</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>weights<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>
weights_norm     <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> weights <span class="hljs-operator">/</span> weights_sum

<span class="hljs-comment"># Step 2g: EAP estimate — posterior mean</span>
theta <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">sum</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>theta_grid <span class="hljs-operator">*</span> weights_norm<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># Step 2h: Posterior standard error</span>
se_theta <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">sqrt</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span><span class="hljs-built_in">sum</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>theta_grid <span class="hljs-operator">-</span> theta<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span><span class="hljs-operator">^</span><span class="hljs-number">2</span> <span class="hljs-operator">*</span> weights_norm<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># Round for display</span>
theta    <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">round</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>theta<span class="hljs-punctuation">,</span> <span class="hljs-number">4</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># ── Diagnostic log ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────</span>
cat<span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span><span class="hljs-string">&quot;\n========================================\n&quot;</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>
cat<span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>sprintf<span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span><span class="hljs-string">&quot;EAP UPDATE after item %d\n&quot;</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">,</span> answered<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>

    answer<span class="hljs-punctuation">,</span> ifelse<span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>is_correct <span class="hljs-operator">==</span> <span class="hljs-number">1</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">,</span> <span class="hljs-string">&quot;CORRECT&quot;</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">,</span> <span class="hljs-string">&quot;INCORRECT&quot;</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>

<h3 id="connect-3">Connect</h3>
<p>Drag from <span class="inline-code-block">showPage - question</span> <span class="strong-block">out</span> → <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span> <span class="strong-block">in</span></p>
<h3 id="details-2">Details</h3>
<p>The <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span> node runs <span class="strong-block">after every submitted answer</span> in the CAT loop. It is the most complex node in the system and performs three sequential tasks:</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Task</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Task 1</span></td><td>Score the response — determine if the answer is correct</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Task 2</span></td><td>Update theta using Bayesian EAP estimation</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Task 3</span></td><td>Check the stopping rule — decide if the test is done</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<hr>

<p><span class="strong-block"><span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span>.<span class="hljs-title function_">numeric</span>()</span></span> is applied defensively because Concerto may pass numeric values as character strings between nodes (e.g., <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-string">&quot;2&quot;</span></span> instead of <span class="inline-code-block">2</span>). Without this conversion, <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-string">&quot;2&quot;</span> + <span class="hljs-number">1</span></span> throws an error in R.</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why fetch from the database again?</span>
The item parameters (<span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">a</span></span></span></span></span>, <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">b</span></span></span></span></span>, <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span></span></span></span></span>) were already available in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - select item</span>, but passing decimal values through Concerto flow variable pointers introduces type corruption risk. Fetching from the database with explicit <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span>.<span class="hljs-title function_">numeric</span>()</span> conversion is safer and always returns the correct type.</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Root cause:</span> Concerto serializes R vectors to disk between loop iterations through flow variable pointers. When deserialized, the vector may arrive in a corrupted form:</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Original value</th><th>What Concerto may return</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">c(0.8, 1.5, 1.2)</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-string">&quot;0.8, 1.5, 1.2&quot;</span></span> (one long string)</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">c(0.8, 1.5, 1.2)</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-title function_">list</span>(<span class="hljs-string">&quot;0.8&quot;</span>, <span class="hljs-string">&quot;1.5&quot;</span>, <span class="hljs-string">&quot;1.2&quot;</span>)</span> (list of strings)</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">c(0.25)</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-string">&quot;0.25&quot;</span></span> (single string)</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">numeric(0)</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block">NULL</span> or <span class="inline-code-block">NA</span></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why use <span class="inline-code-block">length(responses)</span> instead of <span class="inline-code-block">answered</span>?</span></p>

The <span class="inline-code-block">answered</span> variable arrives via flow variable pointer and may have been corrupted during serialization. Using <span class="inline-code-block">length(responses)</span> as ground truth is safer.</p>

<h4 id="task-2-bayesian-eap-theta-estimation">Task 2: Bayesian EAP Theta Estimation</h4>
<h5 id="mathematical-foundation">Mathematical Foundation</h5>
<p>EAP is a Bayesian estimation method. It treats <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span></span></span></span> as a random variable with a prior distribution <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0359em;">π</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span>, combines it with the likelihood of the observed responses, and computes the <span class="strong-block">posterior mean</span> as the estimate.</p>
<p><span class="strong-block">Bayes' theorem:</span></p>
<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">∣</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathbf">u</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:2.4281em;vertical-align:-1.0011em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:1.427em;"><span style="top:-2.305em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mop op-symbol small-op" style="margin-right:0.1945em;position:relative;top:-0.0006em;">∫</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">∣</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mord mathbf">u</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">⋅</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0359em;">π</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace"> </span><span class="mord mathnormal">d</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span></span><span style="top:-3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width:0.04em;"></span></span><span style="top:-3.677em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">∣</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mord mathbf">u</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">⋅</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0359em;">π</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:1.0011em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span></span></span></span></span></div>
<p><span class="strong-block">EAP estimate</span> — posterior mean:</p>
<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.1079em;vertical-align:-0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.9579em;"><span style="top:-3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span><span style="top:-3.2634em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left:-0.1667em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">41</span></span></span></span></span></td><td>41 points</td><td>Standard in IRT software; matches Baker & Kim (2004)</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">numeric(K)</span></td><td>41 zeros</td><td>Pre-allocates the log-likelihood vector</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>

<h6 id="outer-loop--over-grid-points">Outer loop — over grid points</h6>
<p>For each <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8444em;vertical-align:-0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3361em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0278em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.0315em;">k</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> in the grid, computes how likely the observed response pattern is if the test-taker's true ability were <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8444em;vertical-align:-0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3361em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0278em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.0315em;">k</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>.</p>

<p>Clamps <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.9694em;vertical-align:-0.2861em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.1389em;">P</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.1389em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.0572em;">j</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2861em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> to the open interval <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">0.0001</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">0.9999</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> to prevent:</p>

<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6833em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8641em;"></span><span class="mord">0.</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">6</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8641em;"><span style="top:-3.113em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">40</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">1.3</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">×</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8641em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">0</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8641em;"><span style="top:-3.113em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">−</span><span class="mord mtight">9</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></div>
<p>R's floating point minimum is <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4831em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">5</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">×</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8141em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">0</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">−</span><span class="mord mtight">324</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>. Products of many small numbers <span class="strong-block">underflow to zero</span>, making all grid points look equally likely and destroying the estimate.</p>
<p><span class="strong-block">Log transforms products into sums</span> — numerically stable regardless of test length:</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why subtract <span class="inline-code-block">max(log_lik)</span> before <span class="inline-code-block">exp()</span> ?</span></p>
<p>After 10 items, <span class="inline-code-block">log_lik</span> values might range from -30 to -100. <span class="inline-code-block">exp(-100)</span> <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4831em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">3.7</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">×</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8141em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">0</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">−</span><span class="mord mtight">44</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> — very small but still representable. However the <span class="strong-block">relative differences</span> between grid points are what matter for EAP, not the absolute magnitudes.</p>
<p>By centering on the maximum:</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Mathematical justification:</span>
Multiplying all weights by a constant <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7713em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">e</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.7713em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">−</span><span class="mspace mtight" style="margin-right:0.1952em;"></span><span class="mop mtight"><span class="mtight">m</span><span class="mtight">a</span><span class="mtight">x</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> does not change the EAP estimate because the constant cancels in the normalization step:</p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathcal" style="margin-right:0.1474em;">N</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> as prior?</span></p>
<p>This encodes the assumption that, before seeing any responses, the population of test-takers has ability distributed as a standard normal — most people cluster around <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span></span> (average), with fewer at the extremes.</p>
<p><span class="strong-block">Effect of the prior on the estimate:</span></p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Items answered</th><th>Prior influence</th><th>Likelihood influence</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td>1–3</td><td>Strong — pulls theta toward 0</td><td>Weak — little data</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>4–7</td><td>Moderate</td><td>Moderate</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>8–10</td><td>Weak</td><td>Strong — data dominates</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<p>This is exactly what we want: the prior stabilizes estimates early when data is scarce, then gradually yields to the data as evidence accumulates.</p>
<p><span class="strong-block">Prior values across the grid:</span></p>

<p><span class="strong-block">Why <span class="inline-code-block">n_answered</span> not <span class="inline-code-block">answered</span>?</span>
<span class="inline-code-block">n_answered = length(responses)</span> is computed from the actual vector length — immune to serialization corruption. <span class="inline-code-block">answered</span> is a flow variable that has been passed through Concerto and could theoretically be wrong.</p>
<p><span class="strong-block">The <span class="inline-code-block">if</span> node reads <span class="inline-code-block">test_complete</span>:</span>
The <span class="inline-code-block">if</span> node expression is set to <span class="inline-code-block">test_complete</span>. When this is <span class="inline-code-block">TRUE</span>, it routes to <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - compute result</span> → <span class="inline-code-block">showPage - result</span> → <span class="inline-code-block">test end</span>. When <span class="inline-code-block">FALSE</span>, it routes back to <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - select item</span> for the next iteration.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="node-5-if--check-stopping-rule">Node 5: <span class="inline-code-block">if</span> — Check Stopping Rule</h2>
<h3 id="concept-5">Concept</h3>
<p>The stopping rule decides whether to continue the test or end it. We use a <span class="strong-block">fixed-length</span> stopping rule: stop after <span class="inline-code-block">max_items</span> questions <a href="#ref-11">[11]</a><a href="#ref-13">[13]</a>. The <span class="inline-code-block">if</span> node reads the <span class="inline-code-block">test_complete</span> logical variable (TRUE/FALSE) and routes the flow:</p>
<ul>
<li><span class="inline-code-block">TRUE</span> → go to results</li>
<li><span class="inline-code-block">FALSE</span> → loop back, select next item</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="steps-5">Steps</h3>
<ol>
<li>Right-click canvas → <span class="strong-block">if</span></li>
<li>Click the <span class="strong-block">expression</span> input → type:</li>
</ol>

<h2 id="node-6-eval---compute-result--compute-labels-and-confidence-interval">Node 6: <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - compute result</span> — Compute Labels and Confidence Interval</h2>
<h3 id="concept-6">Concept</h3>
<p>Before showing results, this node computes:</p>
<ul>
<li><span class="inline-code-block">ability_label</span> — human-readable interpretation of theta <a href="#ref-5">[5]</a></li>
<li><span class="inline-code-block">ci_lower</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">ci_upper</span> — 95% confidence interval using EAP standard error <a href="#ref-8">[8]</a></li>
<li><span class="inline-code-block">precision_label</span> — description of measurement precision based on SE <a href="#ref-13">[13]</a></li>
</ul>

<li>Drag from <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - compute result</span> <span class="strong-block">out</span> → <span class="inline-code-block">showPage - result</span> <span class="strong-block">in</span></li>
</ul>
<h3 id="details-3">Details</h3>
<p>The <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - compute result</span> node runs <span class="strong-block">exactly once</span> — after the <span class="inline-code-block">if</span> node routes to the <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-literal">true</span></span> port (test is complete). Its purpose is to <span class="strong-block">transform raw numeric outputs</span> from the CAT algorithm into human-readable labels, derived metrics, and formatted values that the results page can display meaningfully.</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Property</th><th>Value</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Runs</span></td><td>Once only — after stopping rule is met</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Position in flow</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block">if</span> (true) → <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - compute result</span> → <span class="inline-code-block">showPage - result</span></td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Purpose</span></td><td>Compute labels, CI bounds, precision assessment, and percentage</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Inputs</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block">theta</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">se_theta</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">answered</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">total_correct</span></td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Outputs</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block">ability_label</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">ci_lower</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">ci_upper</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">precision_label</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">pct_correct</span> + pass-through of inputs</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<hr>
<h4 id="why-this-node-exists-as-a-separate-step">Why This Node Exists as a Separate Step</h4>
<p>It would be technically possible to compute these values inside <span class="inline-code-block">showPage - result</span> using inline JavaScript or inside <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span>. However, separating computation from display follows the <span class="strong-block">separation of concerns</span> principle:</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Reason</th><th>Detail</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Clean display node</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block">showPage - result</span> only handles HTML rendering — no logic</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Testability</span></td><td>Computed values can be logged and inspected before display</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Reusability</span></td><td>The same computed variables can be passed to multiple display nodes if needed</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="strong-block">Concerto limitation</span></td><td>Complex R logic inside <span class="inline-code-block">showPage</span> templates is unreliable</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<hr>

<h6 id="what-it-does-2">What it does</h6>
<p>Maps the continuous theta estimate <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.997em;vertical-align:-0.0391em;"></span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.9579em;"><span style="top:-3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span><span style="top:-3.2634em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left:-0.1667em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">∈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord">−</span><span class="mord">4</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">4</span><span class="mclose">]</span></span></span></span></span> to a discrete categorical label using a set of threshold comparisons.</p>
<h6 id="why-we-need-this">Why we need this</h6>
<p>The raw theta value (e.g., <span class="inline-code-block">0.3821</span>) is meaningful to psychometricians but not to most test-takers. A label like "Average" communicates the result intuitively without requiring knowledge of the IRT scale.</p>
<h6 id="the-threshold-logic">The threshold logic</h6>
<p>R evaluates <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>-<span class="hljs-keyword">else</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span></span> chains top-down and stops at the first <span class="inline-code-block">TRUE</span> condition. The thresholds are based on the standard normal distribution:</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Condition</th><th>Label</th><th>Theta range</th><th>% of population</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">theta &gt;= 2.0</span></td><td>Exceptional</td><td><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord">2.0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">∞</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span></td><td>Top ~2.3%</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">theta &gt;= 1.0</span></td><td>High</td><td><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord">1.0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">2.0</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span></td><td>Next ~13.6%</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">theta &gt;= -1.0</span></td><td>Average</td><td><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord">−</span><span class="mord">1.0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">1.0</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span></td><td>Middle ~68.2%</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">theta &gt;= -2.0</span></td><td>Below Average</td><td><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord">−</span><span class="mord">2.0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">−</span><span class="mord">1.0</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span></td><td>Next ~13.6%</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>else</td><td>Low</td><td><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">−</span><span class="mord">∞</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">−</span><span class="mord">2.0</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span></td><td>Bottom ~2.3%</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<p>These thresholds correspond to the <span class="strong-block">68-95-99.7 rule</span> of the standard normal distribution, since theta is scaled as <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathcal" style="margin-right:0.1474em;">N</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> across the population:</p>

<h6 id="why-else-if-not-multiple-if-statements">Why <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-keyword">else</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span></span> not multiple <span class="inline-code-block">if</span> statements</h6>
<p>Using <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-keyword">if</span>-<span class="hljs-keyword">else</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span></span> ensures <span class="strong-block">only one branch executes</span>. <h6 id="what-it-does-3">What it does</h6>
<p>Computes the <span class="strong-block">95% confidence interval</span> for the theta estimate using the EAP standard error:</p>
<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.9024em;vertical-align:-0.2191em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0715em;">C</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0785em;">I</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3448em;"><span style="top:-2.5198em;margin-left:-0.0785em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">95%</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2191em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.8em;vertical-align:-0.65em;"></span><span class="minner"><span class="mopen delimcenter" style="top:0em;"><span class="delimsizing size2">[</span></span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.9579em;"><span style="top:-3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span><span style="top:-3.2634em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left:-0.1667em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">−</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mord">1.96</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">⋅</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">S</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">E</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3283em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0576em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">E</span><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">A</span><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.1389em;">P</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:1em;"></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.9579em;"><span style="top:-3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span><span style="top:-3.2634em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left:-0.1667em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mord">1.96</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">⋅</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">S</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">E</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3283em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0576em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">E</span><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">A</span><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.1389em;">P</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose delimcenter" style="top:0em;"><span class="delimsizing size2">]</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></div>
<h6 id="why-196">Why 1.96</h6>
<p><span class="inline-code-block">1.96</span> is the <span class="strong-block">critical value</span> of the standard normal distribution at the 95% confidence level:</p>
<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.1389em;">P</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">−</span><span class="mord">1.96</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≤</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8193em;vertical-align:-0.136em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0715em;">Z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≤</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">1.96</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.95</span></span></span></span></span></div>
<p>This means: if we were to repeat the test many times with different random item selections, 95% of the resulting confidence intervals would contain the test-taker's true ability <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span></span></span></span>.</p>
<p>Other common confidence levels:</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Confidence level</th><th>Critical value <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7858em;vertical-align:-0.3552em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.044em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3448em;"><span style="top:-2.5198em;margin-left:-0.044em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.0037em;">α</span><span class="mord mtight">/2</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3552em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></th><th>Code</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td>90%</td><td>1.645</td><td><span class="inline-code-block">theta ± 1.645 * se_theta</span></td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="strong-block">95%</span></td><td><span class="strong-block">1.960</span></td><td><span class="strong-block"><span class="inline-code-block">theta ± 1.96 * se_theta</span></span></td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>99%</td><td>2.576</td><td><span class="inline-code-block">theta ± 2.576 * se_theta</span></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<h6 id="round-3--3-decimal-places"><span class="inline-code-block">round(..., 3)</span> — 3 decimal places</h6>
<p>The CI bounds are rounded to 3 decimal places for clean display. More decimals would imply false precision — given the uncertainty in the estimate, 3 decimal places is sufficient.</p>

                      stroke-linecap="round"
                      stroke-linejoin="round"
                    />
                  </g>
                </svg>
              </button>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div class="pre-code">
          <pre><code id="jb55u" class="r">ci_width <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> ci_upper <span class="hljs-operator">-</span> ci_lower   <span class="hljs-comment"># = 2 * 1.96 * se_theta = 3.92 * se_theta</span></code></pre>
          </div>
          </div>
        
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>SE</th><th>CI width</th><th>Interpretation</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td>0.89 (after Q1)</td><td>3.49</td><td>Covers almost entire scale — very uncertain</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>0.62 (after Q3)</td><td>2.43</td><td>Still very wide</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>0.48 (after Q5)</td><td>1.88</td><td>Moderate</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>0.31 (after Q10)</td><td>1.21</td><td>Reasonably narrow</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>0.20 (target)</td><td>0.78</td><td>High precision</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<p>A CI of width ~1.2 after 10 items is typical for a well-calibrated 3PL CAT.</p>

<h6 id="what-it-does-4">What it does</h6>
<p>Maps the continuous SE value to a categorical precision label, giving test-takers and administrators a plain-language assessment of measurement quality.</p>
<h6 id="the-se-thresholds">The SE thresholds</h6>
<p>The thresholds <span class="inline-code-block">0.3</span> and <span class="inline-code-block">0.5</span> come from the CAT psychometrics literature:</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>SE threshold</th><th>Source</th><th>Meaning</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7224em;vertical-align:-0.0391em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">S</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">E</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">&lt;</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.30</span></span></span></span></span></td><td>Standard CAT stopping criterion</td><td>High precision — equivalent to reliability <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7719em;vertical-align:-0.136em;"></span><span class="mrel">≥</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.91</span></span></span></span></span></td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7224em;vertical-align:-0.0391em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">S</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">E</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">&lt;</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.50</span></span></span></span></span></td><td>Acceptable for many applications</td><td>Moderate precision — class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8193em;vertical-align:-0.136em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">S</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">E</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≥</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.50</span></span></span></span></span></td><td>Below standard</td><td>Low precision — more items needed</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<p><span class="strong-block">Relationship between SE and reliability (<span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.625em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">ρ</span></span></span></span></span>):</span></p>
<p>Reliability is related to SE by:</p>
<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.625em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">ρ</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">−</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8641em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">S</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">E</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8641em;"><span style="top:-3.113em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></div>
<p>(assuming the population variance of theta is 1, i.e., <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.0972em;vertical-align:-0.2831em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0359em;">σ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-2.4169em;margin-left:-0.0359em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span></span></span><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2831em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span></span>)</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>SE</th><th><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8141em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">S</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">E</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></th><th>Reliability <span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.625em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">ρ</span></span></span></span></span></th><th>Label</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td>0.20</td><td>0.04</td><td>0.96</td><td>High precision</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>0.30</td><td>0.09</td><td>0.91</td><td>High precision (boundary)</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>0.40</td><td>0.16</td><td>0.84</td><td>Acceptable precision</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>0.50</td><td>0.25</td><td>0.75</td><td>Acceptable precision (boundary)</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>0.60</td><td>0.36</td><td>0.64</td><td>Low precision</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>0.89</td><td>0.79</td><td>0.21</td><td>Low precision (after Q1)</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>

<h6 id="why-show-this-to-test-takers">Why show this to test-takers?</h6>
<p>Transparency about measurement precision is important in modern assessment. Test-takers deserve to know:</p>
<ul>
<li>How confident the system is in their score</li>
<li>Whether their result is based on sufficient evidence</li>
<li>Whether they might benefit from a longer test</li>
</ul>
<p>In high-stakes contexts, administrators can use this label to flag borderline cases for review.</p>

  precision_label <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> <span class="hljs-string">&quot;High precision&quot;</span>
<span class="hljs-punctuation">}</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">else</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>se_theta <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;</span> <span class="hljs-number">0.40</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">{</span>
  precision_label <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> <span class="hljs-string">&quot;Acceptable precision&quot;</span>
<span class="hljs-punctuation">}</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">else</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">{</span>
  precision_label <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> <span class="hljs-string">&quot;Insufficient precision — retest recommended&quot;</span>
<span class="hljs-punctuation">}</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># Formative assessment (more lenient):</span>
<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>se_theta <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;</span> <span class="hljs-number">0.40</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span> <span class="hljs-punctuation">{</span>

<h6 id="what-it-does-5">What it does</h6>
<p>Computes the percentage of items answered correctly — the classical test theory (CTT) equivalent of the IRT theta estimate.</p>
<div class="math-block"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.9251em;vertical-align:-0.31em;"></span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">pct_correct</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:2.4em;vertical-align:-0.95em;"></span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">round</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="minner"><span class="mopen delimcenter" style="top:0em;"><span class="delimsizing size3">(</span></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:1.427em;"><span style="top:-2.314em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">n</span></span></span><span style="top:-3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width:0.04em;"></span></span><span style="top:-3.677em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mop op-symbol small-op" style="position:relative;top:0em;">∑</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">u</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.0572em;">j</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2861em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.686em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">×</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mord">100</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace"> </span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mclose delimcenter" style="top:0em;"><span class="delimsizing size3">)</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></div>
<p>Where:</p>
<ul>
<li><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.0361em;vertical-align:-0.2861em;"></span><span class="mop op-symbol small-op" style="position:relative;top:0em;">∑</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">u</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.0572em;">j</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2861em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> = <span class="inline-code-block">total_correct</span> — number of correct responses</li>
<li><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">n</span></span></span></span></span> = <span class="inline-code-block">answered</span> — total items answered</li>
<li><span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">×</span><span class="mord">100</span></span></span></span></span> — converts proportion to percentage</li>
<li><span class="inline-code-block">round(..., 1)</span> — rounds to 1 decimal place</li>
</ul>
<h6 id="why-include-this-alongside-theta">Why include this alongside theta?</h6>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>Audience</th><th>Interpretation</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">theta = 0.38</span></td><td>Psychometricians</td><td>Ability on IRT scale</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">pct_correct = 60.0%</span></td><td>Everyone</td><td>6 out of 10 correct</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<p>Most test-takers intuitively understand percentage correct even if they have never heard of IRT. Including both metrics bridges the gap between technical rigor and accessibility.</p>

pct_correct <span class="hljs-operator">&lt;-</span> <span class="hljs-built_in">round</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span><span class="hljs-number">3</span> <span class="hljs-operator">/</span> <span class="hljs-number">7</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span> <span class="hljs-operator">*</span> <span class="hljs-number">100</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">,</span> <span class="hljs-number">1</span><span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>    <span class="hljs-comment"># → 42.9</span></code></pre>
          </div>

<h6 id="why-round-1-not-round-0">Why <span class="inline-code-block">round(..., 1)</span> not <span class="inline-code-block">round(..., 0)</span></h6>
<p>Rounding to 1 decimal place (e.g., <span class="inline-code-block">42.9%</span>) is more informative than rounding to 0 decimals (e.g., <span class="inline-code-block">43%</span>) without implying false precision. For a 10-item test, the minimum distinguishable percentage is 10%, so 1 decimal place is appropriate.</p>
<h6 id="important-note-pct_correct-is-not-the-same-as-theta">Important note: pct_correct is not the same as theta</h6>
<p>Because CAT selects items adaptively, percentage correct is <span class="strong-block">not a fair comparison across test-takers</span>:</p>
<ul>
<li>A high-ability test-taker gets harder items → lower pct_correct despite higher theta</li>
<li>A low-ability test-taker gets easier items → higher pct_correct despite lower theta</li>
</ul>
<p><span class="strong-block">Example:</span></p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Test-taker</th><th><span class="inline-code-block">theta</span></th><th>Items administered</th><th><span class="inline-code-block">pct_correct</span></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td>High ability</td><td>+2.0</td><td>Mostly hard items (<span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">b</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span></span>)</td><td>55%</td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td>Average ability</td><td>0.0</td><td>Mixed items (<span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">b</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span></span>)</td><td>58%</td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td>Low ability</td><td>-2.0</td><td>Mostly easy items (<span class="math-inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">b</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">−</span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span></span>)</td><td>60%</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<p>The low-ability test-taker has the <span class="strong-block">highest</span> percentage correct despite the <span class="strong-block">lowest</span> theta — because they were given easy items they could answer correctly. This is why theta (IRT) is a fairer and more informative measure than raw percentage in adaptive testing.</p>
<p>The <span class="inline-code-block">pct_correct</span> is included as a <span class="strong-block">supplementary familiar metric</span>, not as the primary score. The <span class="inline-code-block">theta</span> estimate is the primary result.</p>
<hr>
<h4 id="why-round-is-applied-here-not-in-eval---score">Why <span class="inline-code-block">round()</span> is Applied Here, Not in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span></h4>
<p>Rounding is applied in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - compute result</span> (the display preparation node) rather than in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span> (the computation node) for an important reason:</p>
<p><span class="strong-block"><span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span> uses <span class="inline-code-block">theta</span> and <span class="inline-code-block">se_theta</span> for further computation in the next loop iteration.</span> If theta were rounded to 3 decimal places inside <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span>, the rounding error would <span class="strong-block">accumulate</span> across 10 iterations:</p>

theta after Q1<span class="hljs-operator">:</span>  <span class="hljs-number">0.382</span>            <span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>rounded<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span>

theta after Q10<span class="hljs-operator">:</span> <span class="hljs-number">0.419</span>            <span class="hljs-punctuation">(</span>accumulated rounding error<span class="hljs-punctuation">)</span></code></pre>
          </div>
          </div>
        
<p>By keeping full precision in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span> and only rounding in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - compute result</span> (which runs after all computation is complete), we eliminate accumulated rounding error.</p>
<p>The <span class="inline-code-block">round()</span> in <span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - score</span> only applies to the <span class="strong-block">final display values</span>:</p>

<hr>
<h5 id="summary-1">Summary</h5>
<p><span class="inline-code-block"><span class="hljs-built_in">eval</span> - compute result</span> is the <span class="strong-block">interpretation layer</span> of the CAT system. It converts raw statistical outputs into meaningful, communicable results:</p>
<div class="data-table-wrapper"><div class="data-table-scroll"><table class="data-table"><thead><tr><th>Input (raw)</th><th>Output (interpreted)</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">theta = 0.3821</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block">ability_label = <span class="hljs-string">&quot;Average&quot;</span></span></td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">theta = 0.3821</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">se_theta = 0.5803</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block">ci_lower = -0.755</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">ci_upper = 1.520</span></td></tr><tr class="even-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">se_theta = 0.5803</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block">precision_label = <span class="hljs-string">&quot;Low precision (more items recommended)&quot;</span></span></td></tr><tr class="odd-row"><td><span class="inline-code-block">total_correct = 6</span>, <span class="inline-code-block">answered = 10</span></td><td><span class="inline-code-block">pct_correct = 60.0</span></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<p>Its design principles are:</p>
<ol>
<li><span class="strong-block">Never modify</span> <span class="inline-code-block">theta</span> or <span class="inline-code-block">se_theta</span> — only compute derived quantities from them</li>
<li><span class="strong-block">Round for display</span> — apply final rounding here, not in computation nodes</li>
<li><span class="strong-block">Pass through</span> all inputs — <span class="inline-code-block">showPage - result</span> needs everything</li>
<li><span class="strong-block">Separate concerns</span> — computation here, rendering in <span class="inline-code-block">showPage - result</span></li>
</ol>

      <span class="hljs-tag">&lt;<span class="hljs-name">strong</span>&gt;</span>How was this score calculated?<span class="hljs-tag">&lt;/<span class="hljs-name">strong</span>&gt;</span><span class="hljs-tag">&lt;<span class="hljs-name">br</span>&gt;</span>
      Your ability estimate (θ̂ = {{theta}}) was computed using
      <span class="hljs-tag">&lt;<span class="hljs-name">strong</span>&gt;</span>Bayesian EAP (Expected A Posteriori)<span class="hljs-tag">&lt;/<span class="hljs-name">strong</span>&gt;</span> estimation
      with the 3-Parameter Logistic (3PL) IRT model.<span class="hljs-tag">&lt;<span class="hljs-name">br</span>&gt;</span><span class="hljs-tag">&lt;<span class="hljs-name">br</span>&gt;</span>
      <span class="hljs-tag">&lt;<span class="hljs-name">strong</span>&gt;</span>What is EAP?<span class="hljs-tag">&lt;/<span class="hljs-name">strong</span>&gt;</span><span class="hljs-tag">&lt;<span class="hljs-name">br</span>&gt;</span>
      EAP combines the likelihood of your response pattern with a standard
      normal prior distribution. The result is the posterior mean — a
      weighted average of the ability scale, where the weights reflect how
      consistent each ability level is with your responses.<span class="hljs-tag">&lt;<span class="hljs-name">br</span>&gt;</span><span class="hljs-tag">&lt;<span class="hljs-name">br</span>&gt;</span>
      <span class="hljs-tag">&lt;<span class="hljs-name">strong</span>&gt;</span>What is SE(θ̂)?<span class="hljs-tag">&lt;/<span class="hljs-name">strong</span>&gt;</span><span class="hljs-tag">&lt;<span class="hljs-name">br</span>&gt;</span>
      The Standard Error ({{se_theta}}) measures estimation precision.
      Values below 0.30 indicate high precision. Your 95% confidence
      interval [{{ci_lower}}, {{ci_upper}}] means we are 95% confident
      your true ability lies within this range.
    <span class="hljs-tag">&lt;/<span class="hljs-name">div</span>&gt;</span>

    <span class="hljs-tag">&lt;<span class="hljs-name">button</span> <span class="hljs-attr">class</span>=<span class="hljs-string">&quot;btn-finish&quot;</span> <span class="hljs-attr">type</span>=<span class="hljs-string">&quot;submit&quot;</span>&gt;</span>Finish<span class="hljs-tag">&lt;/<span class="hljs-name">button</span>&gt;</span>
  <span class="hljs-tag">&lt;/<span class="hljs-name">div</span>&gt;</span>

<span class="hljs-tag">&lt;/<span class="hljs-name">html</span>&gt;</span></code></pre>
